Use `APIRouter` to put related *path operations* in their own modules, then include those routers in your main `FastAPI` app. If you come from Flask, this would be the equivalent of Flask's Blueprints.[2]

**1. Organize files into a package**

```
.
├── app
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── main.py
│   ├── dependencies.py
│   └── routers
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   ├── items.py
│   │   └── users.py
│   └── internal
│       ├── __init__.py
│       └── admin.py
```

There are several `__init__.py` files: one in each directory or subdirectory. This is what allows importing code from one file into another.[2]

**2. Create a router in each module** (e.g. `app/routers/users.py`)

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/users/", tags=["users"])
async def read_users():
    return [{"username": "Rick"}, {"username": "Morty"}]
```

You can think of `APIRouter` as a "mini `FastAPI`" class. All the same options are supported.[4]

**3. Include the routers in `app/main.py`**

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

from .routers import items, users

app = FastAPI()

app.include_router(users.router)
app.include_router(items.router)
```

With `app.include_router()` we can add each `APIRouter` to the main `FastAPI` application. It will include all the routes from that router as part of it.[3] As most of your logic will now live in its own specific module, the main file will be quite simple.[1]

You can also set a `prefix`, `tags`, `dependencies`, and `responses` when including a router, e.g. `app.include_router(admin.router, prefix="/admin", tags=["admin"])`.

**Tip:** Import the submodules, not their `router` variables directly. If we had imported one after the other, like `from .routers.items import router` and `from .routers.users import router`, the `router` from `users` would overwrite the one from `items` and we wouldn't be able to use them at the same time.[5]

You don't have to worry about performance when including routers.[3]

Full guide: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/
